title: Unmapped categories show Parts in the QuickBooks column and sort under P
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with the Settings - Parts permission.
  • {Location-A} is connected to QuickBooks, so the Categories list shows the QuickBooks Products And Services column.
  • Category {Category-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC32 never mapped) has never been mapped to a QuickBooks product or service.
  • QuickBooks product or service {Qb-item-A}, named exactly Parts, exists in the connected QuickBooks company.
  • Category {Category-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC32 mapped to Parts) is mapped to {Qb-item-A}.
  • QuickBooks product or service {Qb-item-B} (for example Equipment) has a name starting with a letter before P.
  • Category {Category-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC32 before P) is mapped to {Qb-item-B}.
  • QuickBooks product or service {Qb-item-C} (for example Services) has a name starting with a letter after P.
  • Category {Category-D} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC32 after P) is mapped to {Qb-item-C}.
  • You are on a page other than Categories.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings and click Categories in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
  2. Find {Category-A} and read its QuickBooks Products And Services cell.
  3. Click the QuickBooks Products And Services column header.
  4. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  5. Read the order of {Category-A}, {Category-B}, {Category-C} and {Category-D}.
  6. Click the QuickBooks Products And Services column header again.
  7. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  8. Read the order of {Category-A}, {Category-B}, {Category-C} and {Category-D}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 2: the cell for {Category-A} reads Parts. It is not empty.
  • Step 5: {Category-C} ({Qb-item-B}) comes first, then {Category-A} and {Category-B} together in the P part of the list, then {Category-D} ({Qb-item-C}). {Category-A} is not moved to the bottom of the list.
  • Step 8: {Category-D} comes first, then {Category-A} and {Category-B} together, then {Category-C}. {Category-A} is again not moved to the bottom.
  • Steps 5 and 8: {Category-A} and {Category-B} cannot be told apart in the QuickBooks column. Both read Parts.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11258; story SV-10134 (Story 1, Categories, sort by name; story text re-synced to the PRD on 13 Oct 2026); PRD "Settings Pricing And Categories Sorting (Price/Category)", Confluence 578781186, version 21 (14 Oct 2026), S1-R17, §4 Key Decisions, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas boards 1.2 (Categories - after) and 2.1 (The three rules that bite), 13 Oct copy, unchanged on 14 Oct. Product comment: Chris Ward, 23 Sep 2026 (Confluence comment 882311473), item 1: test S1-R17 as written. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Price/Category QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R17: “Every category shows a value in the QuickBooks Products and Services column. A category that has never been mapped shows the word Parts there, which is what the page shows today and does not change. That column therefore has no empty state, no row is moved to the bottom of it, and a category showing Parts because it is unmapped sorts under P in the same run as a category whose mapping is genuinely named Parts. The two are indistinguishable in the list, by design.”
  • PRD §4 Key Decisions: “A category that has never been mapped shows the word Parts in that column rather than an empty cell, which is what the page has always done, so there is no empty state there for a rule to act on and unmapped categories sort under P alongside any mapping named Parts.”
